Series::extract_put_¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::extract_put_(pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<ExtractSpec> specs, const Series& values) -> Series&

What It Does¶

Writes into the current series through the full ExtractSpec selector language, mutates in place, and returns *this.

This is the broadest selector-based write surface on Series. If traverse_put_() is the strict “only accept selectors that can remain a pure view” method, extract_put_() is the method that says “accept the full selector grammar and materialize positions when necessary.”

That distinction matters in practice:

  • reverse slices are legal here

  • bool masks are legal here

  • integer advanced indices are legal here

  • mixed selectors that cannot stay a plain view are still legal here

Internally, the selector is normalized, the destination positions are computed, and the final write routes through the explicit index-write machinery. So the mental model is simple even if the lowering path is not:

  • extract() chooses values to read

  • extract_put_() chooses positions to write

Parameters¶

specs (pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<ExtractSpec>)

The destination selector.

This method accepts the same selector language documented for extract(), including:

  • scalar integer indices

  • bounded or unbounded slices

  • negative-step slices

  • SliceAll()

  • Ellipsis()

  • NewAxis()

  • bool mask series

  • integer index series

Write-side selector details:

  • scalar indices consume an existing axis and narrow the addressed region

  • slices keep the axis and choose which positions on it will be written

  • Ellipsis() expands to however many identity slices are required

  • NewAxis() is accepted, but it does not create a new writable axis

  • advanced selectors are materialized into explicit destination positions

values (const Series&)

The source values to assign into the selected destination positions.

Two cardinality rules apply:

  • if values.numel() == 1, the scalar source broadcasts across the entire selection

  • otherwise values.numel() must exactly match the number of selected destination elements

For non-scalar writes, matching is by element count. The source is consumed in the selector’s logical visit order rather than by trying to preserve its original shape.

Returns¶

Series& The same series, after mutation.

Examples¶

Example 1. Shared setup. Start with an ordinary 3 x 4 grid.

auto grid = pluss::make_series(
    {10.0, 11.0, 12.0, 13.0,
     20.0, 21.0, 22.0, 23.0,
     30.0, 31.0, 32.0, 33.0},
    {3, 4});

std::cout << grid;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[3,4], strides=[4,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=12, contiguous=true)
data=[[10, 11, 12, 13],
  [20, 21, 22, 23],
  [30, 31, 32, 33]]

Example 2. A scalar source broadcasts across all selected destinations.

const auto fill_column = std::vector<ExtractSpec>{
    pluss::Slicing::SliceAll(),
    std::int64_t{1}};

grid.extract_put_(
    pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<ExtractSpec>(fill_column),
    pluss::make_series(-1.0));

std::cout << grid;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[3,4], strides=[4,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=12, contiguous=true)
data=[[10, -1, 12, 13],
  [20, -1, 22, 23],
  [30, -1, 32, 33]]

Example 3. Reverse slices are legal here, so write order follows the selector’s logical visitation order.

const auto reverse_write = std::vector<ExtractSpec>{
    std::int64_t{1},
    pluss::Slicing::SliceRange(-1, pluss::Slicing::Slice::kUnbounded, -2)};

grid.extract_put_(
    pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<ExtractSpec>(reverse_write),
    pluss::make_series({90.0, 70.0}, {2}));

std::cout << grid;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[3,4], strides=[4,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=12, contiguous=true)
data=[[10, -1, 12, 13],
  [20, 70, 22, 90],
  [30, -1, 32, 33]]

The selector visits row 1, columns 3 then 1, so 90 lands in column 3 and 70 lands in column 1.

Example 4. NewAxis() is accepted for compatibility with the selector grammar, but it does not create a new writable destination dimension.

const auto with_newaxis = std::vector<ExtractSpec>{
    pluss::Slicing::NewAxis(),
    pluss::Slicing::SliceAll(),
    std::int64_t{0}};

grid.extract_put_(
    pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<ExtractSpec>(with_newaxis),
    pluss::make_series({100.0, 200.0, 300.0}, {3}));

std::cout << grid;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[3,4], strides=[4,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=12, contiguous=true)
data=[[100, -1, 12, 13],
  [200, 70, 22, 90],
  [300, -1, 32, 33]]

Semantically this is still just “write column 0 for every row.”

Example 5. Bool masks are also legal here because extract_put_() is allowed to materialize the addressed positions.

auto row_mask = pluss::make_series({true, false, true}, {3});

const auto mask_specs = std::vector<ExtractSpec>{
    row_mask,
    pluss::Slicing::SliceAll()};

grid.extract_put_(
    pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<ExtractSpec>(mask_specs),
    pluss::make_series(0.0));

std::cout << grid;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[3,4], strides=[4,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=12, contiguous=true)
data=[[0, 0, 0, 0],
  [200, 70, 22, 90],
  [0, 0, 0, 0]]

Example 6. Non-scalar sources must match the selected element count exactly.

try {
  const auto mismatch_specs = std::vector<ExtractSpec>{
      std::int64_t{0},
      pluss::Slicing::SliceRange(0, 4, 2)};

  grid.extract_put_(
      pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<ExtractSpec>(mismatch_specs),
      pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0}, {3}));
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string msg = e.what();
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n'));
}

Output¶

Series::extract_put_: source must be scalar or match selected element count

The selector names only two destination positions, so a three-element source is rejected.

Notes¶

  • extract_put_() is the richest selector-write surface on Series.

  • Use it when the selector may involve masks, reverse traversal, or other non-view addressing.

  • If you want the same write to return a patched copy, use extract_put().

  • If you want the method to reject anything that is not view-representable, use traverse_put_().

See Also¶

  • Series::extract_put: same selector language, but copy-returning.

  • Series::traverse_put_: stricter in-place writes through the view-representable subset only.

  • Series::extract: read-side counterpart.

  • Series::index_put_: explicit index-list writes.
